* Please briefly describe.
Explanation from 2023: 1) The policy needs to be updated in order to follow PSI Directive and strengthen the right to reuse open data through introducing complaint system in case that the user (requester) doesn't get data on request. 2) ambition bar needs to be raised in terms of open data release of high-value datasets 3) Data Officers need to be introduced on all levels of governance (national and local)

Question:

Explanation from 2023: The Office for IT and eGovernment is currently scoping a new project with UNDP Serbia, where the mentioned challenges will be tackled. Additionaly, legislative change is planed as measure of the new Programme for Development of eGovernment for 2023 - 2025
Provide updated explanation (if applicab: The new project focused on open data has started, and it will be implemented by Office for IT and eGovernment, in partnership with UNDP, with support by the United Kingdom. Most of the challenges will be addressed through it. Additionaly, measure for change of the legislative framework has became part of the Programme for development of eGovernment. The new project started in April 2024, and activities which have been implemented up to date are: establishment of the working group for change of the Law on eGovernemnt and Open Data Portal Regulation. Previous to the establishment of the working group, SIGMA has supported consultancy work on Regulatory impact analysis and harmonization with EU PSI Directive and HVD Implementation Act. This has been used as a basis for work of the Working Group. Also, in parallel, we have started cooperation with the Serbian Agency for Environmental Protection to harmonize their open data sets standards with HVD Implementation Act, making them a first institution (pilot), even before it becomes mandatory for all HVD holders.

Question:
Do you have a methodology in place to measure the impact of open data in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the key points of this methodology.
Explanation from 2023:
Methodology is developed in partnership with UNDP, in 2019. URL (linked also on the National Open Data Portal) https://www.undp.org/sr/serbia/publications/potencijalni-uticaj-otvaranja-podataka-u-srbiji  Framework for open data impact indicators  which is proposed in this methodology  is
based on several dimensions.
First the dimension of balancing lead and lag indicators. Lead indicators show whether the right
things to enable open data impact are happening (as no impact would be possible otherwise),
and lag indicators to assess what impact is visible.
Second, establishing indicators along the entire value chain that leads to socio-economic impact
of open data, as apparent from the reviewed research. This value chain runs from data provision,
government efficiency gains, demand and adoption, time and resource investment by external
stakeholders, re-use examples, policy implementation, ecosystem formation, to higher order
usage and network effects.
For the different steps in that chain, both lead and lag indicators can be put forward, along with
the methods to measure them where such experience exists in the research taken into account.
Third, indicators as much as possible should be of the ‘vector’ type (measuring direction and
speed), which more likely leads to more objective measurements. The exact list of indicators is available starting from page 53 of the publication.
